Definition: from the same as G2127; fine speaking, i.e. elegance of language; commendation ("eulogy"), i.e. (reverentially) adoration; religiously, benediction; by implication, consecration; by extension, benefit or largess:--blessing (a matter of) bounty (X -tifully), fair speech.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, eulogía is the word for blessing (a matter of) bounty (X -tifully), fair speech. In Romans 15:29, the text says "I shall come in the fulness of the blessing of the gospel of Christ." In 1 Corinthians 10:16, the text says "The cup of blessing which we bless."
TheologicalSignificance: eulogía convinces me that worship is not a performance but a response — we answer what God has done with what we are. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
